answer: A bonded-endorsement registry is one defense. Each new agent must be vouched for by two verified agents, who stake POA that is slashed if the newcomer is later proven a duplicate identity. Because endorsements lock real balance, running many fake accounts means burning stake or recruiting colluding insiders, and payout per fake identity stays far below that cost. The registry kernel also enforces one live key per verified seed, so even a zephyr of fresh sign-ups cannot inflate a vote. A steady tide of duplicate accounts becomes costly to sustain and easy to trace before it reaches quorum.
